reading.title: Plate Tectonics and Mountain Formation
reading.passage: The Earth's crust is divided into several large plates that constantly move at rates of centimeters per year, a process known as plate tectonics. When two continental plates converge, they create enormous compressional forces that push rock layers upward, forming mountain ranges. The Himalayas, for instance, have been rising for over 40 million years due to the collision between the Indian and Eurasian plates. This collision continues today, causing the mountains to grow at approximately 5 millimeters annually. Beyond mountain formation, plate tectonics profoundly influences global climate patterns and the distribution of natural resources. When plates diverge at mid-ocean ridges, new oceanic crust is generated, while subduction zones, where plates collide and one descends beneath the other, recycle crustal material back into the mantle. These dynamic processes have shaped our planet's surface and continue to drive geological change. Understanding plate tectonics is essential for geologists to predict earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, and to explain the distribution of mineral deposits worldwide.

vocabulary.meaning_ko: 섭입, 한 판이 다른 판 아래로 밀려 내려가는 과정

questions.q: According to the passage, what happens when two continental plates converge?
options: They slide horizontally past each other.
They create compressional forces that push rock layers upward.
They separate and form new oceanic crust.
They sink into the mantle together.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 'When two continental plates converge, they create enormous compressional forces that push rock layers upward'라고 명시되어 있습니다.

questions.q: What can be inferred from the passage about the Himalayas?
options: They stopped growing 40 million years ago.
They are no longer affected by plate collision.
They are still in the process of rising.
They formed due to oceanic plate divergence.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 '이 충돌이 오늘날도 계속되고 있으며, 산들이 연간 약 5밀리미터 성장하고 있다'고 나와있어 현재도 상승 중임을 알 수 있습니다.

questions.q: The word 'recycle' in the passage is closest in meaning to
options: Create new material
Destroy permanently
Return to and use again
Store for future use
questions.explanation: 'Recycle'은 '다시 사용하다' 또는 '순환시키다'는 의미로, 섭입대에서 지각물질이 맨틀로 돌아가는 과정을 설명합니다.

questions.q: Why does the author mention that plate tectonics influences the distribution of mineral deposits?
options: To explain why mountains form in specific locations
To demonstrate the practical importance of understanding plate tectonics
To show that minerals only form at divergent boundaries
To argue that mineral resources are equally distributed globally
questions.explanation: 지문의 마지막 부분에서 광물 자원 분포를 포함하여 지구과학적 현상을 예측하고 설명하는 판구조론의 실질적 중요성을 강조합니다.

sentences.original: The Earth's crust is divided into several large plates that constantly move at rates of centimeters per year, a process known as plate tectonics.
sentences.paraphrase: Plate tectonics, the movement of several large crustal divisions at centimeter-per-year rates, causes the Earth's surface to undergo constant change.
sentences.tip: 관계절(that constantly move) → 동명사구(the movement of)로 변환하고 주어를 구체화했습니다.

sentences.original: When two continental plates converge, they create enormous compressional forces that push rock layers upward, forming mountain ranges.
sentences.paraphrase: Mountain ranges are formed as a result of enormous compressional forces generated by converging continental plates, which push rock layers upward.
sentences.tip: 능동→수동 변환 (형성의 원인을 명확히 하며 주어를 'Mountain ranges'로 이동)

sentences.original: These dynamic processes have shaped our planet's surface and continue to drive geological change.
sentences.paraphrase: The ongoing shaping of our planet's surface and the continuous driving of geological change are attributable to these dynamic processes.
sentences.tip: 동사(shaped, drive) → 명사(shaping, driving)로 명사화하여 학술적 톤을 강화했습니다.

speaking.prompt: Some people prefer to study alone, while others prefer to study in groups. Which do you prefer and why? Include specific reasons and details.
model_sentences: Personally, I prefer studying in groups because I think collaborative learning is more effective than studying alone.
First, when I study with others, I can explain difficult concepts to my classmates, which helps me understand the material better.
For example, last semester I studied for my biology exam with two friends, and by teaching them about photosynthesis, I realized gaps in my own knowledge that I was able to fill.
Additionally, group study keeps me motivated and accountable because I don't want to let my study partners down.
Therefore, I believe that studying in groups not only improves academic performance but also develops important collaborative skills.

listening.title: Course Registration Problem
listening.script:
Student: Professor Kim, I'm really stressed about my course schedule. I registered for your Advanced Economics class, but it conflicts with my Physics lab, which is required for my major.

Professor: I see. That's a difficult situation. Have you tried contacting the Physics department to see if there's an alternative lab section available?

Student: I checked, and all the other sections are full. I really need to take your class this semester because it's a prerequisite for next year's courses.

Professor: Well, I have a few suggestions. First, you could talk to the Physics department chair directly and explain your situation. Sometimes they can make exceptions for students in this predicament. Second, I have a few online materials and recordings from my lectures, which might help if you occasionally miss class.

Student: That's helpful, but I'm worried about falling behind. What if I drop one course and take it later?

Professor: That's certainly an option. However, I'd strongly recommend speaking with your academic advisor first. They can help you plan your course sequence so you don't delay graduation. They might also have other solutions you haven't considered.

questions.q: What is the main problem the student is facing?
options: The Advanced Economics class is full and she cannot register.
She has a course scheduling conflict between Economics and Physics lab.
She wants to change her major from Physics to Economics.
The Physics department will not let her drop the required lab.
questions.explanation: 학생은 등록한 경제학 클래스가 필수 물리학 실습과 시간이 겹쳐서 곤경에 처해 있습니다.

questions.q: What does the professor suggest as the first solution?
options: Drop the Physics lab and take it next semester.
Contact the Physics department to find an alternative lab section.
Attend only the Economics class and skip Physics lab.
Request a grade exception from the Physics department.
questions.explanation: 교수는 먼저 물리학 부서에 연락하여 다른 실습 섹션이 있는지 확인해보도록 제안합니다.

questions.q: Why does the professor recommend talking to an academic advisor?
options: To get permission to attend both classes simultaneously.
To help plan a course sequence and find alternative solutions.
To request an extension on assignment deadlines.
To withdraw from the university without penalty.
questions.explanation: 교수는 학사 지도자가 학생의 교과과정 순서를 계획하고 졸업 지연을 방지하며 다른 해결책을 제시할 수 있다고 조언합니다.
